title: Reject a valid compressed partial backup
goal: Diagnose tar-to-gzip pipeline failure, retaining the real partial candidate and creating a separate verified retry.
challenge: Demonstrate a failed archive producer followed by successful compression. Prove the first gzip stream is valid but incomplete; retain it, then build and restore a different complete candidate without changing sources.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/textarchive-composition.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/textarchive-composition.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh source original.sha partial.tar.gz stages.txt complete.tar.gz complete.sha members.txt restore && mkdir source && printf 'alpha\n' > source/alpha.txt && printf 'beta\n' > source/beta.txt && sha256sum source/alpha.txt source/beta.txt > original.sha
steps.explanation: A missing requested member will cause the producer to fail, but downstream gzip can still write a valid stream. Keep originals and the failed candidate.

steps.command: here && dir_ok source && { timeout -k 1s 8s tar -cf - -C source -- alpha.txt absent.txt 2>/dev/null | timeout -k 1s 8s gzip -n > partial.tar.gz; ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"); printf '%s\n' "${ps[*]}" > stages.txt; test "${ps[0]}" != 0 && test "${ps[1]}" = 0; } && gzip -t partial.tar.gz && tar -tzf partial.tar.gz
steps.explanation: Redirection and compression are not transactional. gzip CRC validates that stream, not completeness or expected source data. Save every stage status immediately.
steps.expected: Partial archive exists and gzip testing passes, despite a failing tar stage.

steps.command: here && dir_ok source && { timeout -k 1s 8s tar -cf - -C source -- alpha.txt beta.txt | timeout -k 1s 8s gzip -n > complete.tar.gz; ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"); test "${ps[*]}" = '0 0'; } && test "$(stat -c %s complete.tar.gz)" -le 65536 && sha256sum complete.tar.gz > complete.sha && tar -tzf complete.tar.gz > members.txt && cmp members.txt <(printf 'alpha.txt\nbeta.txt\n') && fresh restore && mkdir restore && dir_ok restore && timeout -k 1s 8s tar -xzf complete.tar.gz -C restore --no-same-owner --same-permissions && cmp source/alpha.txt restore/alpha.txt && cmp source/beta.txt restore/beta.txt && sha256sum -c original.sha complete.sha
steps.explanation: The retry gets a new filename and destination. Compare declared members and independent content expectations; never accept an earlier failed output merely because it decompresses.
steps.expected: Both complete restored files match, failed candidate remains and originals are unchanged.

hints: Inspect the producer status, not just gzip -t.
A retry should preserve the failed candidate and use a fresh destination.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0: partial 103.4 pipeline/error evidence; 103.3/105.2 reinforcement. LPIC-2 v4.5.0: related 206.2 recovery reinforcement only. Self-reviewed and unscored; no full coverage.
